- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) after a recent peak, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days post-sentiment shift.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, especially when sentiment flips sharply; dampen forecast volatility by 15–25% if sentiment changes >0.5 in 3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% for next 5 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Overshoot after spikes (especially >75% above prior high) is common; cap forecast at 10% below prior peak if sentiment remains neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish cycles with low volatility, model tends to overestimate; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast variance by 10–15%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of forecast’s 10-day moving average, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days unless sentiment confirms breakout.
